title: Parallel merge sort

blocks.text: The page's Q2 builds `MergeSortTask extends RecursiveTask<int[]>`, which **returns** the sorted values:

items: Base case: if `array.length <= threshold`, sort a **copy** with `Arrays.sort` and return it.

Otherwise copy the left and right halves into their own arrays, make a task for each, run them (the page forks the left, computes the right and joins the left), and **merge** the two sorted halves into one new array.

blocks.text: Write `MergeSortTask(array, threshold)`. The caller's array is never changed, and the task never hands it back as its result.

rows: a new array `1, 2, 3`; the input still reads `3, 1, 2`
a new array `7`, not the input itself

cases.says: The task returns the values in ascending order and leaves the input as it was.
An array no longer than the threshold, even a single value, is sorted into a new array; the input is not changed or returned.
Equal values from the two halves are all kept by the merge.
An empty input gives a new empty array, not the input object.
With threshold 1 a one-element range is the base case, so the sort ends and is correct.

concepts: A merge-sort RecursiveTask returns a new sorted array, merging the two sorted halves it joined.
